sources.title: Charles M. Grinstead and J. Laurie Snell, Introduction to Probability
sources.locator: Chapter 11 §§11.2–11.5, especially printed pp. 416–428; absorbing canonical form, finite-step escape, fundamental matrix, hitting probabilities, mean exit time, finite communicating classes, and Cesàro/periodic behavior.

read_evidence.method: Retrieved the complete 518-page book PDF and inspected the relevant full-text arguments: §11.2 Theorems 11.3–11.6 and the Drunkard’s Walk calculation, plus §11.3 Example 11.16 and stationary-law passages. Local items prove the graph algorithm, multi-class decomposition, and residual extensions beyond the source hypotheses.

contents.name: §11.2, finite-step absorption and canonical absorbing form
contents.support: The source motivates the finite path-to-exit argument; the item constructs the common L and epsilon directly from finitely many positive paths.

contents.name: §11.2, fundamental matrix, absorption probabilities, and mean absorption time
contents.support: The item proves the Neumann inverse, the first-exit path sum, the expectation tail identity, and both residual bounds under its explicit escape hypothesis.

contents.name: §§11.3–11.5, finite communicating classes, stationary laws, and periodic chains
contents.support: The item proves the closed-class mixture, first-entry weights, and Cesàro convergence with its own finite-state argument.

contents.name: §11.2 absorbing-chain example and exact first-step equations
contents.support: The example independently verifies the finite credit chain's hitting probabilities, mean exit times, escape constants, and residual estimate by exact arithmetic.

contents.name: §11.1 finite transition convention
contents.support: The row-kernel convention is transposed explicitly to the local column convention; the definition itself states all matrix identities needed here.

contents.name: §11.2 absorbing-chain path and canonical-form context
contents.locator: §11.2, Definition 11.1 and canonical form, printed pp. 416–418
contents.support: The source gives the absorbing/transient block context; the local Floyd-style reachability procedure and its correctness are proved here.

contents.name: §11.2 finite-step escape argument
contents.support: The source uses finite paths to an absorbing state to derive uniform finite-step escape; the local theorem proves the multi-closed-class graph path property and applies the same finite path principle.

contents.name: §11.3 invariant laws for finite irreducible chains
contents.locator: §11.3, Theorem 11.10 and surrounding fixed-vector discussion, printed pp. 438–445
contents.support: The local proof derives positivity and uniqueness for every finite irreducible class directly and does not import an aperiodic convergence claim.

contents.name: §11.2 canonical absorbing form
contents.support: The block form motivates the transient/closed split; the local proof establishes fixed-space dimension and the all-row augmentation claim.

contents.name: §11.3 periodic two-state example
contents.support: The source identifies an irreducible periodic chain whose powers do not become regular; the local example computes the oscillation and lazified coefficient exactly.

contents.name: §11.2 identity/reducible boundary
contents.locator: §11.2 absorbing-chain setup and §11.3 invariant-law discussion, printed pp. 416–445
contents.support: The example’s two singleton classes and complete stationary family are verified locally by exact calculation.

contents.name: §11.3 finite birth–death invariant-law context
contents.support: The local example computes the uniformized matrix, pairwise detailed-balance flows, stationary vector, and contraction coefficient exactly.

sources.title: Ilse C. F. Ipsen and Teresa M. Selee, Ergodicity Coefficients Defined by Vector Norms
sources.locator: Complete 48-page paper; §3, Theorem 3.7 and Corollary 3.9, PDF pp. 12–13 (printed pp. 164–165); induced zero-sum l1 coefficient and pairwise row-distance/overlap formula, transposed to columns.

read_evidence.method: Retrieved the complete 48-page paper and read the complete §3 proof of Theorem 3.7 and Corollary 3.9, including the zero-sum restriction, pairwise row-distance formula, overlap identity, and row-to-column transpose used locally.

contents.name: Theorem 3.7 and Corollary 3.9: exact l1 coefficient on zero-sum vectors and overlap formula
contents.support: The item gives a complete column-convention derivation from positive/negative probability masses and proves both the maximum column-distance and minimum-overlap formulas.

contents.name: §3: nonexpansiveness of stochastic matrices in the vector l1 norm
contents.support: The item proves mass preservation and l1 nonexpansiveness directly from finite sums and nonnegative column entries.

contents.name: Theorem 3.7 and Corollary 3.9 applied to powers of a stochastic matrix
contents.support: The local proof uses the coefficient for P^m and proves uniqueness, the stationary residual estimate, and the one-step telescoping bound.

contents.name: §3 one-norm stochastic contraction
contents.support: The local proof gives the column-convention mass preservation and l1 nonexpansiveness by finite sums.

contents.name: §3 zero-sum coefficient and column-overlap formula
contents.support: The local proof derives the column formulas from positive/negative probability masses and checks the one-state case.

contents.name: §3 coefficient for powers and stationary residual control
contents.support: The algorithm computes the finite column-overlap coefficient of P^m exactly and exposes certificate-unavailable when it is not below one.

contents.name: §3 zero-sum contraction and residual bound
contents.support: The residual theorem supplies the zero-sum contraction ingredient; the local proof adds algorithm termination and the explicit correction ledger.

contents.name: §3 zero-sum contraction after uniformization
contents.support: The local corollary substitutes the exact identity Qx/ν=Px−x under the proved uniformization hypotheses.

contents.name: §3 perturbation coefficient context for generator error
contents.support: The contraction factor is used for the true generator; the local proof separates computed residual and model discrepancy by a triangle inequality.

contents.name: §3 exact nearly-reducible two-state coefficient
contents.support: The example computes the column overlap and proves the residual bound is sharp by rational arithmetic.

contents.name: §3 exact permutation and identical-column endpoints
contents.support: The local example evaluates coefficient one for the swap and zero for the lazy matrix directly.

sources.title: Yuanyuan Liu, Perturbation Bounds for the Stationary Distributions of Markov Chains
sources.locator: Complete paper; §1 equations (1.1)–(1.4), PDF pp. 1–2, and §2.1 Lemma 2.1 with its complete proof, PDF pp. 4–5; stationary sensitivity and periodic m-skeleton coefficient.

read_evidence.method: Retrieved the complete paper and read §1 equations (1.1)–(1.4) and the complete §2.1 proof of Lemma 2.1, including the m-skeleton argument for periodic chains. The local finite-state residual and model-error arguments are proved in their assigned items.

contents.name: Equations (1.1)–(1.4): stationary-distribution sensitivity through an ergodicity coefficient
contents.support: The assigned proof derives its residual version directly and states the m-step coefficient needed when one-step contraction fails.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1 and complete proof: coefficient restriction to the periodic m-skeleton
contents.support: The local result uses the actual power P^m and does not assume aperiodicity or convergence of ordinary powers.

contents.name: Stationary perturbation decomposition into a solve residual and model discrepancy
contents.support: The local ledger proves the exact triangle-inequality split between the computed-model residual and the true-generator discrepancy at the corrected candidate.

contents.name: §1 stationary perturbation and residual equations
contents.support: The computed procedure keeps the stationary residual distinct from how the candidate was generated; the correction and coefficient calculations are proved locally.

contents.name: §2.1 m-skeleton contraction proof
contents.locator: §2.1, Lemma 2.1 and complete proof, PDF pp. 4–5
contents.support: The source’s skeleton argument supports use of P^m when ordinary one-step contraction fails; the local theorem supplies the exact finite-state bound.

contents.name: §1 stationary sensitivity under a model perturbation
contents.support: The local result specializes transition-matrix sensitivity to a finite uniformized generator and states the exact ν scaling.

contents.name: §1 solve-residual and perturbation separation
contents.support: The local proof decomposes Qx into the computed model residual and true-model discrepancy at the corrected candidate.
